THE FINDING THE RELEASE OWNER MOST NEEDS, unchanged and now measured in both directions: THE MODERN EDITION OF ULYSSES IS A REWRITE, NOT A NORMALISATION, AND IT CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH. Episode 1 showed it deleting names (Chrysostomos at 1:9, Mercury's hat at 1:293, Chuck Loyola at 1:101) and substituting them (Swinburne for Algy, William for Billy). EPISODE 3 SHOWS IT DOING THE OPPOSITE: it NAMES FOUR PEOPLE JOYCE DID NOT NAME -- Aristotle at 3:0 (the older edition has only 'but he adds: in bodies'), Brian Boru at 3:57 (Joyce wrote 'the Dalcassians', which is a people and not a man), Deasy at 3:10, and Queen Victoria at 3:94 (the older edition has only 'the old hag with the yellow teeth'). BRIAN BORU IS THEREFORE AN ENTITY THAT EXISTS IN THE MODERN EDITION ALONE and is an omittedEntity for the ORIGINAL edition -- the inverse of Chrysostomos and Mercury, and the first such case in this library. It also respells Ferrando as Fernando, Patk MacCabe as Patrick, Haroun al Raschid as Rashid, Dan Occam as William of Ockham, Joachim Abbas as Joachim of Fiore and Columbanus as Saint Columban. Check both editions before writing any card that turns on a name.

THE DISCIPLINE THAT MATTERS MOST HERE, and it paid again: LIST EVERY OCCURRENCE OF A NAME ACROSS ALL 18 EPISODES BEFORE CHOOSING BETWEEN AN ALIAS AND A KEY. In episode 3 it found that RICHIE is Stephen's uncle here and RICHARD SHAKESPEARE at 9:375 and 9:391 ('nuncle Richie and nuncle Edmund'); that PAT is Kevin Egan's son at 3:59 and bald Pat the waiter through the whole of episode 11; that WALTER is Richie's crosseyed son here and Walter Sexton, Sir Walter Raleigh and Walter Bapty elsewhere; that SARA is the aunt here and Sara Curran at 12:172; that MALACHI at 3:67 is the HIGH KING who wore the collar of gold and not Buck Mulligan, so the book-wide alias had to be suppressed there; and that TANDY IS TWO MEN INSIDE THIS ONE EPISODE -- master Shapland Tandy at 3:19 and Napper Tandy at 3:59. It also reached BACK INTO EPISODE 2, which had been signed off: the fiery COLUMBANUS is at 2:73 and was not cast. He binds there now. Do not undo any of these.

A MECHANICAL TRAP THAT IS SILENT AND COSTS A WHOLE CARD: '_Los Demiurgos_' at 3:1 sits inside Gutenberg italic underscores, and the shared alias binder in reviewed_aliases.py guards its matches with \w, WHICH AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES -- so the name could not be bound by alias at all and nothing reported it. The keyed tables guard with [A-Za-z] instead and reach it, so the demiurge is bound as a phrase. ANY ALIAS IN THIS LIBRARY WHOSE ONLY OCCURRENCE IS INSIDE _ITALICS_ IS INVISIBLE IN EXACTLY THIS WAY, in every book, not just this one.

FOURTEEN PEOPLE IN EPISODE 3 ARE NAMED ONLY BY A DESCRIPTION and are bound on the phrase the text uses: the cocklepicker and his woman, the girl at the bookshop window, the two Marys, Kevin Egan's wife, the froeken at Upsala, the Bruce's brother, the cornet player, the bishop of Cloyne, Mulligan's aunt at 3:53 and 3:54, and the man who was drowned -- the same man the cliff watchers were waiting for in episode 1. THE HEAD CENTRE IS THE HARDEST: the text names him by his office and never by his name, and the card says so rather than supplying the name from outside the book. Deliberate gaps, each pinned by a test: 'by the law Harry' at 3:27 is an oath; Tatters at 3:72 is a dog; delta of Cassiopeia at 3:82 is a star; Madeline the mare at 3:2 is a horse and is NOT the Madeleine of Rodot's at 3:56; Houyhnhnm at 3:35 is a species used as an adjective; and the Swift of 'a hater of his kind' and 'Abbas father, furious dean' is never named and is left unbound.
